newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thais dismiss judge for corruption in drug case.
newsitem.headline: Thais dismiss judge for corruption in drug case.

text.p: Thai judicial officials on Monday voted to dismiss a senior Thai judge who granted bail to the man accused of masterminding the biggest heroin haul in U.S. history, judicial officials said.

An 11-member committee voted unanimously to dismiss Somchai Udomwong, the Deputy Chief Justice of the Criminal Court, without pension for signing a February 7 order freeing Li Yun-chung on five million baht ($192,308) bail.
Investigations had been under way by the committee since March when it was discovered that Li had jumped bail and fled to Burma.

"There were reasonable grounds to believe he was involved in corruption relating to Li," one member of the judicial committee told Reuters. "If the judicial branch finds that somebody is dishonest or guilty of misconduct, he must be removed."
Li was sent back to Thailand by the Rangoon government in May. Earlier this month he was extradited to the United States and arraigned in a Brooklyn Federal Court on drug trafficking changes.
Li was accused of being responsible for importing a 1,070 lb (486 kg) shipment of heroin to the United States in 1991 with a street value of $1 billion.
The drugs from the "Golden Triangle", where Laos, Thailand and Cambodia meet, were seized in Oakland, California, during a routing customs check. They were believed to be destined for New York.
